sections.body: Before you believe or share something, check it in at least 2 TRUSTED sources: a reliable encyclopedia, a museum, a science organisation, a well-known news outlet.
Ask: Who wrote it? Do they have evidence? When was it written? Does it make me feel very angry or excited? Strong feelings can be a warning sign.
Pictures can be edited or taken out of context. A reverse image search (with an adult) can show where a picture really came from.

quiz.q: You read a surprising 'fact' on a random website. What should you do?
hints: How many trusted sources should agree?
If a friend said there's no school tomorrow, you'd check with your teacher or school website before believing it.
quiz.explain: Check it in at least 2 trusted sources first.

quiz.q: A post makes you feel VERY angry and says 'Share before it's deleted!'. This is…
options: A warning sign it might be misleading
hints: Why would someone want you to rush?
Strong feelings stop us thinking carefully.
Scam messages say 'Act now!' to stop people checking. This uses the same trick.
quiz.explain: Pressure and strong emotion are warning signs. Slow down and check.
